verses.1: My son, if you have become surety for your neighbor, you have given your hand to a stranger.
verses.2: You have ensnared yourself by the words of your mouth, you have been caught by the words of your mouth.
verses.3: Do this, my son, and be rescued: because you have come into the grasp of your friend. Go, be bold and rouse your friend who trusted you.
verses.4: Do not let sleep fall on your eyes, nor slumber on your eyelids.
verses.5: Rescue yourself, like a gazelle from the hand, like a bird from the hand of the fowler.
verses.6: Go to the ant, you lazy one, observe her ways and become wise.
verses.7: She has no master, no overseer or ruler.
verses.8: She prepares her food in the summer, she gathers her provisions in the harvest.
verses.9: How long will you lie down, you lazy one? When will you rise from your sleep?
verses.10: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to lie down.
verses.11: Then poverty will come to you like a wanderer, and need like one armed.
verses.12: A man of no sense walks along with iniquity, his mouth speaks perverse things.
verses.13: His glance he winks, with his foot he signals; with his fingers he gestures.
verses.14: Deceit is in his heart, he plots evil constantly, spreading strife.
verses.15: Therefore sudden destruction will come upon him, and a break without remedy.
verses.16: These six things the Lord hates, and seven are an abomination to his soul.
verses.17: Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood,
verses.18: a heart that plots evil, feet that run to do evil,
verses.19: a false witness who speaks lies, and one who stirs up strife among brothers.
verses.20: My son, keep your father’s command, and do not forsake your mother’s teaching.
verses.21: Let them remain bound on your heart always; let them be tied around your neck.
verses.22: When you walk, it will guide you, when you sleep it will guard you, and when you wake it will speak with you.
verses.23: For a lamp is the command, and the teaching is light, and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life.
verses.24: To keep you from an evil woman, from the smooth tongue of a foreigner.
verses.25: Do not let your heart be drawn to her beauty, do not let her eyes ensnare you.
verses.26: For the price of a prostitute is as much as a single loaf, but a woman who takes a man’s life will hunt him.
verses.27: Can a man carry fire in his bosom and his clothes not be burned?
verses.28: Or can one walk on hot coals and his feet not be scorched?
verses.29: So is the one who goes to a married woman; he will not remain unpunished. No one who touches her will go free.
verses.30: It is not considered a disgrace for a thief to steal, if he steals to satisfy his hunger.
verses.31: But if he is caught, he will pay sevenfold; he will give all the wealth of his house.
verses.32: The one who commits adultery is a foolish heart; he who destroys himself will do so.
verses.33: He will find wounds and disgrace, and his shame will not be wiped out.
verses.34: For a man’s jealousy is a burning fire, and he will not show mercy on the day of reckoning.
verses.35: He will not take a bribe at all, nor will he be appeased, though many gifts are offered.

notes:
Notes
- v. 16: "These six things the Lord hates, and seven are an abomination to his soul" — the structure implies a list of seven, but the text says six "things" and seven "abominations," which is a minor textual ambiguity. The translation follows the text as written.
